claims.claim: Unity Catalog uses a three-level namespace, catalog.schema.table, and two-part names resolve against the current catalog.
spark.catalog.currentCatalog() returns the current catalog (PySpark 3.4 and later).
claims.source: Present on PySpark 4.0.4 in this repository.

concept_html:
Unity Catalog names every table with three parts: catalog.schema.table.

research_prod.research_silver.nat_respondents

Use each level for one purpose:

  • Catalog = environment (or a major business domain): research_dev, research_test, research_prod. Permissions and storage attach at this level, so a dev job with no rights on research_prod cannot damage it.
  • Schema = layer or subject: research_bronze, research_silver, research_gold, research_governance.
  • Table = content at a stated grain: nat_raw, nat_respondents, nat_metrics.

Always write the full three-part name in pipeline code, built from configuration. A two-part name such as research_silver.nat_respondents resolves against the session's current catalog. That depends on the workspace default, a USE CATALOG somewhere earlier in the notebook, or a job setting. The same code then reads a different table in each place it runs.

Build names in one function from config, so no code concatenates strings on its own:

def table_name(catalog: str, layer: str, tracker: str) -> str:
    suffix = {"bronze": "raw", "silver": "respondents", "gold": "metrics"}[layer]
    return f"{catalog}.research_{layer}.{tracker}_{suffix}"

In a notebook, spark.catalog.currentCatalog() tells you which catalog a two-part name would use. It is useful for checks, never as a substitute for naming the catalog.

Workspaces created before Unity Catalog also show hive_metastore, the legacy two-level store. Treat it as read-only history while you migrate.

lines: LAYER_SUFFIX = {"bronze": "raw", "silver": "respondents", "gold": "metrics"}
def table_name(catalog: str, layer: str, tracker: str) -> str:
"""Three-level table name for a tracker and layer.
Raises:
KeyError: If layer is not bronze, silver or gold.
"""
return f"{catalog}.research_{layer}.{tracker}_{LAYER_SUFFIX[layer]}"
def load_silver(spark: SparkSession, cfg: RunConfig) -> DataFrame:
"""Read the silver table for the configured environment and tracker."""
return spark.table(table_name(cfg.catalog, "silver", cfg.tracker))

exercises.solution:
LAYER_SUFFIX = {"bronze": "raw", "silver": "respondents", "gold": "metrics"}


def table_name(catalog: str, layer: str, tracker: str) -> str:
    """Three-level Unity Catalog name for a tracker's table in one layer.

    Args:
        catalog: Environment catalog, for example research_dev.
        layer: bronze, silver or gold.
        tracker: Tracker short name, for example nat.

    Returns:
        The fully qualified table name.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the layer is unknown or the catalog contains a dot.
    """
    if "." in catalog:
        raise ValueError(f"catalog must be a single name, got {catalog!r}")
    if layer not in LAYER_SUFFIX:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown layer {layer!r}")
    return f"{catalog}.research_{layer}.{tracker}_{LAYER_SUFFIX[layer]}"

title: The three-level namespace, one catalog per environment
why_html:
A shared all-purpose cluster has research_prod as its default catalog. A developer tests a silver fix from a notebook that writes to research_silver.nat_respondents, a two-part name, believing the notebook "runs in dev". The MERGE lands in production. The fix was only half finished, and 1,400 rows get wrong region codes before anyone notices.

With a three-part name built from a dev config file, the same notebook writes to research_dev.research_silver.nat_respondents. The developer's lack of MODIFY on research_prod would also have blocked it.
